public class RReal extends SysMLAttributeType implements Serializable
SysMLinJava value type for the SysML Real represented by a java double value

This representation of the real number type is for a generic real as used in SysML. Hence the use of a Java double for its value. This SysML real is not the same as the java float, double, Float or Double types as SysML does not discriminate between bit-lengths of real or floating- point numeric types as the Java language does.

Note that the Real name is used by SysML/UML to represent real numbers. To prevent any confusion between this SysML Real and its representation in SysMLinJava, the double R is used in the RReal name, consistent with the double letters used for SysMLinJava's BBoolean, IInteger, and SString value types.

Note: as an ObservableValue this value type can be "observed" by other objects. ValueObservers call the addValueObserver() operation to be notiified (called-back) by the RReal object of any change in its value. This notification will only occur if and when the RReal value is changed by a call to the setValue() operation. So, while the RReal.value is publicly accessible and can be changed by direct assignment, the setValue() operation must be used if ValueObservers are to be automatically notified of the change.

      protected void createUnits()
      Description copied from class: SysMLAttributeType
      Required operation to create/assign the units attribute for this attribute type. The units variable should be assigned with the name of a SysMLUnit instance located in an extension of the SysMLUnits class. An example is as follows: 
      @Override
protected void createUnits()
{
        units = SysMLinJavaUnits.FeetCubic;
}
